name: h1b
_comment: H1b (BF_TREE_V2_PLAN.md): the copy-on-access second chance landed in
c99c040 and was never swept.  Axes are the reference's own
(benchmark/bench_bftree.toml): copy-on-access 0..100 percent of the ring,
read promotion 1..100 percent.  The full cross product would take over a
day at the 900 s steady-state warmup, so this runs two one-dimensional
sweeps through the defaults (copy-on-access 10, promotion 30) on a shape
where steady state is cheap: a 32 MiB budget against 4M rows cycles the
ring within seconds (evictions > 0 inside a 4 s warmup, 2026-09-24
liveness check), so a 120 s warmup is saturated.  Verify that per cell:
read cached_records and evictions beside every hit rate (rule 9).
bf_shed (-DSQLITE_BF_UPGRADE_SHED, opt-in) crosses the copy-on-access
axis: shedding cold records on size upgrades is the other half of the
reference's cold discard.  stock runs once per experiment as the fixed
reference (it ignores both knobs).
Promotion is deterministic since 2dc8f8c (fixed-seed xorshift), so the
two repeats differ only by machine noise, not by promotion draws.
Tripwire, NOT QUOTABLE (8 s runs, v100, 32 MiB ring): copy-on-access
0/10/40/100 -> mini_page_hits 1.51M/1.73M/1.77M/1.21M, cached_records
179k/159k/120k/44k, evictions 156k/208k/402k/1.66M.  Prediction to test:
an interior optimum; strict LRU (100) churns the ring.
